Subject: EU-only processing: operator access + purge path for inference (Schrems II + SCCs)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. EuroPharm is preparing our procurement checklist for EU-only processing under the SCCs and we have a couple of follow-ups specifically for inference workloads. We want to make sure your answers map into our DPA and operator-access appendix. High-level asks:

- Confirmation that inference requests (prompt text and generated outputs) from our EU tenant are processed and persisted only in EU-resident compute and storage.
- How operator/admin access is scoped (does operator access ever cross borders via support tools?). Which roles can access logs or query data for debugging?
- Persistence: what is your retention guarantee for KV cache, temporary caches, and long-term logs? Is there a purge API and can we obtain evidence of deletion?
- Backups and subprocessors: are backups stored outside the EU? Which subprocessors may receive EU customer data?

Can you provide a short evidence bundle (one-page statement + any operator access matrix + a simple diagram of the purge path for inference caches/replicas)? Legal wants this by COB Monday (Oct 4) to feed into our SCCS evaluation.

Thanks,
Marie
Marie Dupont
Head of Cloud Security
EuroPharm Ltd

Hi Marie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, we'll follow with a one-page evidence bundle and matrix:

1) EU-only processing: Yes — for a EuroPharm tenant we can pin inference execution and short-term storage to in-region (EU-West/Frankfurt or EU-North/Stockholm) compute pools and object stores. Model weights and runtime are hosted on EU hardware when tenant is configured for "EU-only".

2) Operator access: Operators and SREs by default are role-scoped; support sessions that require access to logs are gated by an approvals workflow and logged. Some privileged tooling is accessible from our global control plane but operators must authenticate via our SSO and access is limited to the tenant's region scope for data plane views. We will include a role-by-role operator access matrix.

3) Persistence & purge: KV caches (per-request transient cache + session cache) are ephemeral (TTL configurable, default 1 hour) and never replicated to backups; we keep request logs and audit trails for 90 days by default, configurable per contract. We provide a purge API and a deletion attestation flow for targeted keys.

4) Backups & subprocessors: Backups for EU-only tenancy are kept in-region; any cross-border subprocessors are listed and covered by SCCs and contractual obligations.

Ben and Hannah are copied to add the technical and contractual artifacts. I'll also upload a short diagram and matrix to the shared drive and send an attestation PDF. Will aim to get the bundle to you by EOD.

Best,
Irene

Marie / Irene — quick technical addendum to the above so Legal has concrete controls to reference: 

- Compute and storage: when tenant is set to EU-only we schedule inference jobs onto EU-located GPU pools and attach EU object buckets encrypted with customer-dedicated KMS keys (if requested). Model artifacts are not migrated outside region.

- KV / caches: we maintain three classes: 1) per-request transient buffers (ephemeral, destroyed on completion), 2) short-session KV cache (TTL default 1 hour; configurable to 0), and 3) persistent telemetry/logs (retention 90 days default). Short-session caches are in-memory on node and are not backed up to object storage. We have an explicit purge endpoint (/v1/admin/tenants/{tenant}/purge) that invalidates KV entries and triggers a background sweep. We can provide a signed deletion event log for a purge request.

- Backups: snapshot backups of long-term logs are stored in-region; these backups are encrypted and access-controlled. Cross-border movement only occurs for aggregated telemetry for product analytics and is pseudonymized; raw customer data is not exported.

- Operator tooling: operator sessions that require debugging may use a read-only view into request traces; any sensitive payloads are masked by default. Access requires MFA + Just-In-Time approval from the security approver. We maintain per-operator audit trails.

I'm attaching a matrix that maps roles->allowed actions->scope (in-region vs control-plane).

Attachments: sccs_operator_access_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Let me know if you want this table embedded into the DPA or as a separate appendix.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Marie — attaching the one-page statement and the purge flow diagram that maps the inference path (request -> KV cache -> ephemeral node -> purge sweep -> deletion attestation). The PDF includes our standard SCCs operator-access wording and suggested DPA appendix language.

Key points in the bundle:
- Operational guarantee: when "EU-only" flag is on, data plane (compute and object storage) is pinned to EU regions; evidence includes region logs and KMS key IDs.
- Purge path: purge API call returns a job id; upon completion we emit a signed deletion record to the tenant's audit channel; retention of the deletion evidence is 1 year by default (can be extended contractually).
- Operator access matrix: only named operator roles can request just-in-time elevated access and those sessions require an approval ticket and are time-limited.

Next steps I propose: 1) we add the operator access matrix as an appendix to the DPA; 2) Redwood provides a sample deletion evidence PDF for one purge job by Oct 8; 3) schedule a 30-min call with your legal and cloud security to confirm wording.

Attachments: eu_inference_purge_flow_v1.pdf (diagram + attestation template)

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
